facts.text: The '2' in Zombi 2 is a cheat: Dawn of the Dead was released in Italy as Zombi, so producers sold this as its sequel. Fulci said he didn't know about the title and was displeased.
The script began as 'Nightmare Island,' a riff on The Island of Doctor Moreau, written before Dawn of the Dead hit Italy. The New York scenes were added later.
Enzo G. Castellari was offered the director's chair first. He passed because he didn't feel right for a horror film, and Lucio Fulci got the job as the second choice.
Ian McCulloch got the lead because producer Ugo Tucci loved the BBC series Survivors, which was a hit in Italy.
The cast mixed English and Italian speakers, and there was no live sound. Everyone was dubbed afterward, so lips and lines never quite match in any language.
Several actors' contracts promised trailers. None were there when shooting began, and only Richard Johnson talked the producers into providing one.
Richard Johnson was reportedly considered for James Bond in Dr. No (1962). He turned down the multi-picture contract and later played a Bond-ish Bulldog Drummond.
The shark-vs-zombie fight was producer Ugo Tucci's idea. It was shot by makeup wizard Giannetto De Rossi in Mexico without Fulci's approval, and Fulci reportedly thought it was ridiculous.
The underwater zombie was a real shark trainer, because the scheduled actor fell ill. The tiger shark was reportedly fed beforehand and sedated to keep it calm.
Fulci reportedly called the extras in their caked-on, multi-layer zombie makeup 'walking flower pots.'
Composer Fabio Frizzi's score for the eye-gouging scene was inspired by the Beatles' 'A Day in the Life.' He also added Caribbean cues meant to 'pleasantly deceive' the audience.
Frizzi said that after first seeing the eye-splinter scene, he asked editor Vincenzo Tomassi where it was cut, to be sure it was an effect and not real.
Makeup artist Rosario Prestopino said Olga Karlatos ran to her dressing room in tears after watching footage of her character's death. The eye shot used a life mask with a prosthetic eye.
The Italian premiere was in Rome on 25 August 1979. It outgrossed Romero's Dawn of the Dead in Italy, which led to an official Zombi 3.
Zombi 2 cost about 410 million lire and reportedly grossed over 3 billion worldwide, roughly seven times its budget.
Screenwriter Dardano Sacchetti took his name off the credits after his father died during preproduction. A film about the dead rising felt too close to home.
The main title theme reportedly reuses music from the soundtrack of the 1977 Godzilla remix known as 'Cozzilla.'
Tisa Farrow's sister is Mia Farrow, and the Beatles' 'Dear Prudence' was written about her other sister, Prudence.
Tisa Farrow died January 10, 2024. Dawn of the Dead star David Emge died ten days later.
Lucio Fulci used to be a medical student and an art critic before becoming a filmmaker.
The UK cut 1 minute 46 seconds for its 1980 release. Then it landed on the 'video nasties' list, and the BBFC didn't pass it uncut until 2005.
Fulci had three films on the original UK video nasties list: Zombie, The Beyond, and The House by the Cemetery.
The US release was unrated because the MPAA would have given it an X. Promo material reportedly included airline vomit bags.
Fulci appears in a cameo as Peter's news editor.
Zombie was nominated for the Saturn Award for Best Make-up at the 8th Saturn Awards in 1981.
The film inspired the games Dead Island and Dead Island: Riptide, which are also about escaping a zombie outbreak on a tropical island.
Jay Baruchel wears a 'Zombie vs. Shark' t-shirt in This Is the End (2013).
Entertainment Weekly ranked Zombie #10 on its 'Guilty Pleasures: Testosterone Edition' list in 2007.
Fulci began directing Zombi 3 but illness forced him to hand over to Bruno Mattei and Claudio Fragasso.
